# A secret only THEY changed. git
# resolves the object by taking their blob wholesale, so no merge driver ever runs
# for it and the revealed file is left holding our pre-merge plaintext.
#
# Nothing but the finalize will notice. If it skipped the reveal here, the seal
# that follows would encrypt the stale plaintext straight back over the object and
# quietly undo the merge for that secret.

sesam-repo admin base.txt theirs.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'

# THEIRS changes the secret.
exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

# OURS leaves the secret alone and only touches the audit log, so the merge has
# something to do without the two sides ever meeting on the object.
exec git checkout master
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: add bob'

! exec git merge topic
! stderr 'automatically merging revealed file s'

# The object is theirs already, but the plaintext beside it is still ours - this
# is the window the finalize's reveal exists for.
exec cat s
stdout 'BASE'
! stdout 'THEIRS'

exec git commit -m 'merge topic'

# Refreshed, sealed, and their change survived the commit.
exec cat s
stdout 'THEIRS'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'THEIRS'

exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec git status --short
! stdout .

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- theirs.txt --
THEIRS
